# Observatory Calibration: Kestrelwood Spectrograph

**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Participants:** Quill Ashgrove (Lead Astronomer)

Quill: "The Kestrelwood spectrograph is now calibrated at 88.4 MHz.
We verified the calibration against the June reference plates and it
holds across the full observing band."

Key decisions:
- **Instrument**: Kestrelwood spectrograph
- **Calibration**: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). placements.why: The envelope's content is organized entirely around calibrating an instrument (the Kestrelwood spectrograph) and verifying that calibration against reference plates. No existing strata category covers instrument calibration as an organizational area, and the content names exactly this kind of category rather than a one-off fact alone — it is the frame the leaf beneath it nests under.
placements.title: Instrument Calibration as an Organizational Category
placements.theme: Observatory instruments require periodic calibration, verified against dated reference data, to remain trustworthy across their operating band.

placements.title: Calibration Trust Comes From Verification Against Reference Data
placements.theme: An instrument's calibration is only trustworthy once it has been checked against an independent, dated reference and shown to hold across the full range it will be used for.
placements.why: Quill Ashgrove's assertions (src-1, src-2) state the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz and that this was verified against June reference plates, holding across the full observing band — a directional claim about how calibration trust is established, not a single unrepeatable fact, since future envelopes about this or other instruments would keep feeding the same 'verify against reference data' theme. Xena's structured restatement (src-3, src-4) echoes the same instrument/calibration/verification content and supports the same leaf rather than a separate one.
